connections.disconnect.description: Sidebar › Connections: right-click menu of a saved server. Every tab on that server goes to the home folder.

connections.duplicate.description: Sidebar › Connections: right-click menu of a saved server. A copy of the connection, opened to be edited.

connections.duplicate_name.description: The name a duplicated connection gets. {name} is the original's name, as "Home NAS".

connections.edit.description: Sidebar › Connections: tooltip of an icon button above the list. Also in a server's right-click menu. Edits the chosen connection, or renames the chosen folder. "..." means a dialog opens.

connections.empty.description: Sidebar › Connections while no server is saved.

connections.error.no_server.description: Error when OK is pressed in the Connection dialog with the Server field empty.

connections.error.port.description: Error when the Port field of the Connection dialog holds no number. {text} is what was typed, as "22a".

connections.field.access_key.description: Label left of a field in the Connection dialog (a saved server's details). Keep it short: the label column is narrow. S3: the access key ID, which stands for the user.

connections.field.api_key.description: Label left of a field in the Connection dialog (a saved server's details). Keep it short: the label column is narrow. Rackspace Cloud Files (Swift): the API key, which stands for the password.

connections.field.application_key.description: Label left of a field in the Connection dialog (a saved server's details). Keep it short: the label column is narrow. Backblaze B2: the application key, which stands for the password.

connections.field.bucket.description: Label left of a field in the Connection dialog (a saved server's details). Keep it short: the label column is narrow. S3 and B2: the bucket, and a folder in it, to start in.

connections.field.container.description: Label left of a field in the Connection dialog (a saved server's details). Keep it short: the label column is narrow. Rackspace Cloud Files (Swift): the container, and a folder in it, to start in.

connections.field.endpoint.description: Label left of a field in the Connection dialog (a saved server's details). Keep it short: the label column is narrow. S3: the storage service's server address.

connections.field.key_id.description: Label left of a field in the Connection dialog (a saved server's details). Keep it short: the label column is narrow. Backblaze B2: the application key's ID, which stands for the user.

connections.field.name.description: Label left of a field in the Connection dialog (a saved server's details). Keep it short: the label column is narrow. The name the Connections list shows.

connections.field.password.description: Label left of a field in the Connection dialog (a saved server's details). Keep it short: the label column is narrow.

connections.field.port.description: Label left of a field in the Connection dialog (a saved server's details). Keep it short: the label column is narrow. The network port number.

connections.field.region.description: The Connection dialog, S3 only: the label of the region field (AWS's eu-central-1 and the like). Keep it short.

connections.field.secret_key.description: Label left of a field in the Connection dialog (a saved server's details). Keep it short: the label column is narrow. S3: the secret access key, which stands for the password.

connections.field.server.description: Label left of a field in the Connection dialog (a saved server's details). Keep it short: the label column is narrow. The server's host name or address.

connections.field.start_folder.description: Label left of a field in the Connection dialog (a saved server's details). Keep it short: the label column is narrow. The folder shown after logging in.

connections.field.user.description: Label left of a field in the Connection dialog (a saved server's details). Keep it short: the label column is narrow. The user name to log in with.

connections.folder.delete_title.description: Title of the question before deleting a folder of Sidebar › Connections that holds connections.

connections.folder.exists.description: Error naming a folder of Sidebar › Connections as another one. {name} is the name typed, as "Work".

connections.folder.name.description: Label of the name field in the New Folder and Rename Folder dialogs of Sidebar › Connections.

connections.folder.new_title.description: Title of the dialog naming a new folder of Sidebar › Connections (it groups connections; not a folder on a disk).

connections.folder.rename.description: Sidebar › Connections: right-click menu of a folder grouping connections. "..." means a dialog opens.

connections.folder.rename_title.description: Title of the dialog renaming a folder of Sidebar › Connections (it groups connections; not a folder on a disk).

connections.move_down.description: Sidebar › Connections: tooltip of an icon button above the list. Moves the chosen connection or folder one place down.

connections.move_to_folder.description: Sidebar › Connections: tooltip of an icon button above the list. Opens a list of the folders to move the chosen connection into.

connections.move_up.description: Sidebar › Connections: tooltip of an icon button above the list. Moves the chosen connection or folder one place up.

connections.new.description: Sidebar › Connections: tooltip of an icon button above the list. Also in a folder's right-click menu. Opens the Connection dialog for a new server. "..." means a dialog opens.

connections.new_folder.description: Sidebar › Connections: tooltip of an icon button above the list. Makes a folder to group connections in the list (not a folder on a disk). "..." means a dialog opens.

connections.no_folder.description: First item of Move to Folder's list: the top of the Connections list, outside any folder.

connections.open_in_terminal.description: Sidebar › Connections: right-click menu of a saved server. For SFTP servers: logs in with ssh in the terminal pane.

connections.password.delete.description: Tooltip of the trash can button inside the Password field of the Connection dialog: deletes the password saved for this server.

connections.password.delete_button.description: Confirming button of the Delete Password dialog. Keep it short.

connections.password.delete_confirm.description: Question of the Delete Password dialog. Once deleted, the password is asked for each time the server is connected to.

connections.password.delete_title.description: Title of the dialog confirming that the password saved for a server is deleted (trash can button in the Connection dialog).

connections.password.not_read.description: Error after the eye button of the Connection dialog's Password field could not read the saved password (the keyring did not answer, or it is locked).
connections.password.not_read.message: The saved password could not be read.

connections.placeholder.name.description: Grey hint inside the empty field of the Connection dialog, saying what an empty field means; lower case. Name field.

connections.placeholder.password.description: Grey hint inside the empty Password field of the Connection dialog when no password is saved for the server; lower case. The password is asked for when connecting.

connections.placeholder.password_saved.description: Grey hint inside the empty Password field of the Connection dialog when a password is saved for the server; lower case. Left empty, the saved one stays; one typed replaces it.

connections.placeholder.path.description: Grey hint inside the empty field of the Connection dialog, saying what an empty field means; lower case. Start folder field: empty, the folder the server starts in after logging in.

connections.placeholder.port.description: Grey hint inside the empty field of the Connection dialog, saying what an empty field means; lower case. Port field: empty, the protocol's usual port is used.

connections.placeholder.region.description: Grey hint inside the empty Region field of the Connection dialog (S3), saying what an empty field means; lower case. Empty, the region comes from the endpoint's name (s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com), else us-east-1 is used. Keep us-east-1 as it is.

connections.placeholder.server.description: Grey hint inside the empty field of the Connection dialog, saying what an empty field means; lower case. Server field: a host name, or the name of a Host in the user's SSH configuration. Keep ~/.ssh/config as it is.

connections.placeholder.user.description: Grey hint inside the empty field of the Connection dialog, saying what an empty field means; lower case. User field: empty, SSH's configuration names the user, and FTP logs in anonymously. Keep ~/.ssh/config as it is.

connections.save_failed.description: Error writing the saved servers to the settings folder. {err} is the system's own error text.

connections.ssh_config.read_only.description: Tooltip of the ~/.ssh/config heading in Sidebar › Connections, which lists the hosts of the user's SSH configuration file. Keep ~/.ssh/config as it is.
connections.ssh_config.read_only.message: Read only: these hosts are edited in ~/.ssh/config itself

main.admin.button.description: Button: do it again as administrator; the system then asks for the password. Keep it short.

main.admin.deleting.description: What permission refused, before ": permission denied. As administrator, …": {count} files or folders left undeleted, e.g. 3.
main.admin.deleting.message: Deleting {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}

main.admin.failed.description: Notification: doing it as administrator failed too. {err} is the reason, e.g. "Not authorized".

main.admin.making.description: What permission refused, before ": permission denied. As administrator, …": a new folder. {name} is its name, e.g. "Backup".

main.admin.offer.description: Text of the Permission denied dialog. {what} is what was refused, e.g. 'Making "Backup"' or 'Renaming to "notes.txt"'.
main.admin.offer.message: {what}: permission denied. As administrator, the system asks for the password.

main.admin.offer_delete.description: Text of the Permission denied dialog for a deletion (no trash then). {what} is what was refused, e.g. "Deleting 3 items".
main.admin.offer_delete.message: {what}: permission denied. As administrator, the system asks for the password. What is deleted so is gone for good.

main.admin.title.description: Title of the dialog offering to do something as administrator after the system refused it.

main.delete.from_archive.description: Delete dialog inside an archive (no trash there). {archive} is the archive's name, e.g. "backup.zip". kind is "folder" or "file" for one chosen entry, its name in {name} (e.g. "Photos"); "other" for several, {count} of them (e.g. 3).
main.delete.from_archive.message: {kind, select, folder {Delete the folder "{name}" from {archive}? This cannot be undone.} file {Delete the file "{name}" from {archive}? This cannot be undone.} other {Delete {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} from {archive}? This cannot be undone.}}

main.delete.on_server.description: Delete dialog on a server (no trash there). {server} is its address, e.g. "sftp://me@nas". kind is "folder" or "file" for one chosen entry, its name in {name} (e.g. "Photos"); "other" for several, {count} of them (e.g. 3).
main.delete.on_server.message: {kind, select, folder {Delete the folder "{name}" on {server}? This cannot be undone.} file {Delete the file "{name}" on {server}? This cannot be undone.} other {Delete {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} on {server}? This cannot be undone.}}

main.delete.permanently.description: Delete permanently dialog: deleted without the trash. kind is "folder" or "file" for one chosen entry, its name in {name} (e.g. "Photos"); "other" for several, {count} of them (e.g. 3).
main.delete.permanently.message: {kind, select, folder {Delete the folder "{name}" permanently? This cannot be undone.} file {Delete the file "{name}" permanently? This cannot be undone.} other {Delete {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} permanently? This cannot be undone.}}

main.delete.title.description: Title and confirming button of the dialog asking whether to delete. Keep it short.

main.delete.title_permanently.description: Title and confirming button of the dialog asking whether to delete without the trash (Shift+Delete). Keep it short.

main.delete.to_trash.description: Delete dialog: the chosen entries go to the trash. kind is "folder" or "file" for one chosen entry, its name in {name} (e.g. "Photos"); "other" for several, {count} of them (e.g. 3).
main.delete.to_trash.message: {kind, select, folder {Move the folder "{name}" to the trash?} file {Move the file "{name}" to the trash?} other {Move {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} to the trash?}}

main.download.view.description: A task in the operations queue: a server's file is downloaded to show it in the viewer. {file} is its name, e.g. "report.pdf".

main.error.make_folder.description: Notification: a new folder (F7) could not be made. {err} is the reason, e.g. "Photos exists already".

main.error.read_settings.description: Notification at start: the settings file could not be read, so the defaults are used. {err} is the reason.

main.error.read_workspaces.description: Notification at start: the saved workspaces (named sets of tabs) could not be read. {err} is the reason.

main.error.save_settings.description: Notification: the settings file could not be written. {err} is the reason, e.g. "No space left on device".

main.folder_tree.home.description: Sidebar › Folders: the tree's first root, the user's home folder. Keep it short.

main.new_folder.title.description: Title of the dialog asking a new folder's name (F7).

main.undo.queued.description: Notification: undoing (way is "undo") or redoing (way is "redo") a move waits in the operations queue. {title} is the operation, e.g. "Move 3 items to /home/me".
main.undo.queued.message: {way, select, redo {In the queue to redo: {title}} other {In the queue to undo: {title}}}

quick_view.extracting.description: Quick View panel, while a file is unpacked from an archive to be shown.
quick_view.extracting.message: Taking it out of the archive…

quick_view.files_only.description: Quick View panel, when the cursor is on a folder on a server or in an archive.
quick_view.files_only.message: On servers and inside archives, Quick View shows files.

quick_view.space.title.description: Quick View panel on a folder, as Total Commander's: the line above the totals.

quick_view.space.totals.description: Quick View panel on a folder: what is in it; bytes, files and folders = the counts, each *_grouped the same with its digits grouped, e.g. 1 234 567.
quick_view.space.totals.message: {bytes, plural, one {{bytes_grouped} byte} other {{bytes_grouped} bytes}} in {files, plural, one {{files_grouped} file} other {{files_grouped} files}}, {folders, plural, one {{folders_grouped} folder} other {{folders_grouped} folders}}

quick_view.space.unreadable.description: Quick View panel on a folder: how many files or folders could not be read, e.g. 3.

quick_view.too_large.download.description: Quick View panel; size = the file's size, e.g. 1.2 GB. F3 is the key of the viewer.
quick_view.too_large.download.message: {size} is too large to download here: F3 views it.

quick_view.too_large.extract.description: Quick View panel; size = the file's size, e.g. 1.2 GB. F3 is the key of the viewer.
quick_view.too_large.extract.message: {size} is too large to take out of the archive here: F3 views it.

remote.cancelled.description: Error when the password or passphrase dialog was cancelled, shown after the server's name and a colon, as "nas.lan: cancelled". Starts in lower case: it is shown after a name and a colon.

remote.cloud.ask.description: Text of the dialog asking the secret of an online storage, one choice per service (see remote.cloud.title). {user} is the key ID, access key or user, as "AKIAEXAMPLE"; {host} the server, as "s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com". Translate each choice.
remote.cloud.ask.message: {kind, select, application_key {Application key of {user} at {host}:} api_key {API key of {user} at {host}:} password {Password of {user} at {host}:} other {Secret key of {user} at {host}:}}

remote.cloud.ask_again.description: As remote.cloud.ask, asked again after the service refused the secret given. {user} is the key ID, access key or user, as "AKIAEXAMPLE"; {host} the server, as "s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com". Translate each choice.
remote.cloud.ask_again.message: {kind, select, application_key {Wrong application key. Application key of {user} at {host}:} api_key {Wrong API key. API key of {user} at {host}:} password {Wrong password. Password of {user} at {host}:} other {Wrong key. Secret key of {user} at {host}:}}

remote.cloud.obscure_failed.description: Error connecting to a WebDAV server through rclone, when rclone failed to encode the password.
remote.cloud.obscure_failed.message: rclone could not take the password

remote.cloud.rclone_missing.description: Error connecting to online storage without the rclone add-on. Settings > Add-ons is the page of the Settings dialog that downloads it.
remote.cloud.rclone_missing.message: rclone is missing: Settings > Add-ons downloads it

remote.cloud.title.description: Title of the dialog asking the secret of an online storage (through rclone): Backblaze B2's application key, Rackspace Cloud Files' API key, WebDAV's password, or S3's secret key. Translate each choice.
remote.cloud.title.message: {kind, select, application_key {Application key} api_key {API key} password {Password} other {Secret key}}

remote.connecting.description: Note while connecting to a server or share. {server} is its host name or address, as "nas.lan" or "smb://nas/media".

remote.dialog.cancel.description: Button of the dialogs connecting to a server (password, login, unknown server) and of the Connection dialog.

remote.dialog.ok.description: Button of the dialogs connecting to a server (password, login, unknown server) and of the Connection dialog.

remote.disconnect_failed.description: Error letting go of a network share. {share} is its address or folder, as "smb://nas/media"; {err} the system's own error text.

remote.ftp.password.description: Text of the dialog asking an FTP server's password. {user}@{host} is the login, as "me@ftp.example.org": keep the @ between them.

remote.ftp.password_again.description: Text of the dialog asking an FTP server's password again after a wrong one. {user}@{host} is the login, as "me@ftp.example.org": keep the @ between them.

remote.ftps.changed.description: Security error connecting to an FTPS server whose certificate differs from the one recorded. {server} is the server and port, as "ftp.example.org:21"; {line} a line number; {file} the path of the file of known certificates. CHANGED is in capitals for emphasis.
remote.ftps.changed.message: The TLS certificate of {server} has CHANGED since line {line} of {file} recorded it. Someone could be listening in; if the server has a new certificate, remove that line.

remote.ftps.not_trusted.description: Error connecting to an FTPS server whose TLS certificate was not accepted. Starts in lower case: it is shown after a name and a colon.
remote.ftps.not_trusted.message: the server's certificate is not trusted

remote.login.password.description: Label of the password field in the Log in dialog. Keep it short: the label column is narrow.

remote.login.title.description: Title of the dialog asking a network share's (SMB, WebDAV) user and password after it refused to open.

remote.login.user.description: Label of the user name field in the Log in dialog. Keep it short: the label column is narrow.

remote.mount.login_wrong.description: Error opening a network share (SMB, NFS, WebDAV), shown after its address and a colon, as "smb://nas/media: …". Starts in lower case: it is shown after a name and a colon.
remote.mount.login_wrong.message: the user or password is wrong

remote.mount.macos_failed.description: Error opening a network share (SMB, NFS, WebDAV), shown after its address and a colon, as "smb://nas/media: …". Starts in lower case: it is shown after a name and a colon. macOS only. {code} is NetFS's error number, as "-5999".

remote.mount.needs_desktop.description: Error opening a network share (SMB, NFS, WebDAV), shown after its address and a colon, as "smb://nas/media: …". Starts in lower case: it is shown after a name and a colon. kio-fuse and gvfs are programs' names.
remote.mount.needs_desktop.message: needs KDE's kio-fuse or GNOME's gvfs

remote.mount.needs_login.description: Error opening a network share (SMB, NFS, WebDAV), shown after its address and a colon, as "smb://nas/media: …". Starts in lower case: it is shown after a name and a colon.
remote.mount.needs_login.message: it needs a user and password

remote.mount.no_fuse.description: Error opening a network share (SMB, NFS, WebDAV), shown after its address and a colon, as "smb://nas/media: …". Starts in lower case: it is shown after a name and a colon. gvfs-fuse is a program's name.
remote.mount.no_fuse.message: mounted, but there is no folder for it: gvfs-fuse is missing

remote.mount.no_nfs_client.description: Error opening a network share (SMB, NFS, WebDAV), shown after its address and a colon, as "smb://nas/media: …". Starts in lower case: it is shown after a name and a colon. Windows only: "Client for NFS" and "Windows Features" are Windows' own names; use Windows' names in your language.
remote.mount.no_nfs_client.message: not found; NFS needs Windows' Client for NFS (Windows Features)

remote.mount.no_share.description: Error opening a network share (SMB, NFS, WebDAV), shown after its address and a colon, as "smb://nas/media: …". Starts in lower case: it is shown after a name and a colon. The address has no share after the server; smb://server/share shows the form it needs.

remote.mount.not_address.description: Error opening a network share (SMB, NFS, WebDAV), shown after its address and a colon, as "smb://nas/media: …". Starts in lower case: it is shown after a name and a colon. macOS only.

remote.mount.not_found.description: Error opening a network share (SMB, NFS, WebDAV), shown after its address and a colon, as "smb://nas/media: …". Starts in lower case: it is shown after a name and a colon. macOS only: the share mounted, but its folder was not found.
remote.mount.not_found.message: mounted, but not found among the mounted

remote.mount.other_user.description: Error opening a network share (SMB, NFS, WebDAV), shown after its address and a colon, as "smb://nas/media: …". Starts in lower case: it is shown after a name and a colon. Windows only.
remote.mount.other_user.message: Windows is connected to this server as another user: log off, or use that user

remote.password.title.description: Title of the dialog asking an SFTP or FTP server's password.

remote.remember_password.description: Checkbox in the password and login dialogs: keeps the password. Settings › Passwords is the page of the Settings dialog where kept passwords are.

remote.save_back_failed.description: Error after a server's file was edited in an external editor: the changed file could not be uploaded to the server. {err} is the reason.

remote.sftp.host_certificate.description: Error connecting to an SFTP server that identifies itself with an SSH host certificate instead of a host key.
remote.sftp.host_certificate.message: The server shows a host certificate; those are not supported yet.

remote.sftp.key_changed.description: Security error connecting to an SFTP server whose key differs from the one recorded. {server} is the server, as "nas.lan" or "nas.lan:2222"; {line} a line number; {file} the known_hosts file's path. CHANGED is in capitals for emphasis.
remote.sftp.key_changed.message: The host key of {server} has CHANGED since line {line} of {file} recorded it. Someone could be listening in; if the server was set up anew, remove that line.

remote.sftp.key_not_trusted.description: Error when the user did not accept an SFTP server's unknown key. {server} is the server, as "nas.lan" or "nas.lan:2222".
remote.sftp.key_not_trusted.message: The host key of {server} was not trusted.

remote.sftp.keys_refused.description: Error connecting to an SFTP server. {user}@{host} is the login, as "me@nas.lan": keep the @ between them.
remote.sftp.keys_refused.message: {user}@{host}: the server refused the keys and takes no password

remote.sftp.login_refused.description: Error connecting to an SFTP server after wrong passwords. {user}@{host} is the login, as "me@nas.lan": keep the @ between them.

remote.sftp.passphrase.description: Text of the dialog asking the passphrase of an encrypted SSH key file. {file} is the key file's path, as "/home/me/.ssh/id_ed25519".

remote.sftp.passphrase_title.description: Title of the dialog asking the passphrase of an encrypted SSH key file.

remote.sftp.password.description: Text of the dialog asking an SFTP server's password. {user}@{host} is the login, as "me@nas.lan": keep the @ between them.

remote.unknown_host.once.description: Unknown server dialog button: trusts the server's key for this connection only.

remote.unknown_host.remember.description: Unknown server dialog button: trusts the server's key from now on.

remote.unknown_host.text.description: Text of the Unknown server dialog. {host} is the server, as "nas.lan" or "ftp.example.org:21"; {key_type} is "TLS" for an FTPS server's certificate (the first choice), else the SSH key's algorithm, as "ssh-ed25519" (the other choice; keep it as it is); {fingerprint} is the key's digest, as "SHA256:3f9a…". Translate both choices; keep the empty lines.

remote.unknown_host.title.description: Title of the dialog asking whether to trust a server seen for the first time.

rename.case.description: Multi-Rename Tool: the label before the capital-letter choices. Keep it short.

rename.case.first.description: Multi-Rename Tool: a Case choice, only the name's first letter a capital. Keep it short.

rename.case.lower.description: Multi-Rename Tool: a Case choice, all letters made small; written as it does. Keep it short.

rename.case.unchanged.description: Multi-Rename Tool: a Case choice, the names' letters kept as they are. Keep it short.

rename.case.upper.description: Multi-Rename Tool: a Case choice, all letters made capitals; written as it does. Keep it short.

rename.case.words.description: Multi-Rename Tool: a Case choice, each word's first letter a capital; written as it does. Keep it short.

rename.close.description: Multi-Rename Tool: the button that closes it. Keep it short.

rename.counter_start.description: Multi-Rename Tool: the label above the counter's first number. Keep it short.

rename.dialog_title.description: Title of the Multi-Rename Tool dialog (Ctrl+M), as Total Commander's.

rename.digits.description: Multi-Rename Tool: the label above the counter's number of digits. Keep it short.

rename.extension.description: Multi-Rename Tool: the label above the extension mask field. Keep it short.

rename.field.counter.description: Multi-Rename Tool: a button that puts [C], the counter, into the mask. Keep [C] as it is. Keep it short.

rename.field.date.description: Multi-Rename Tool: a button that puts the file's date (year, month, day) into the mask. Keep [Y][M][D] as it is. Keep it short.

rename.field.extension.description: Multi-Rename Tool: a button that puts [E], the old extension, into the mask. Keep [E] as it is. Keep it short.

rename.field.folder.description: Multi-Rename Tool: a button that puts [P], the folder's name, into the mask. Keep [P] as it is. Keep it short.

rename.field.name.description: Multi-Rename Tool: a button that puts [N], the old name, into the mask. Keep [N] as it is. Keep it short.

rename.field.range.description: Multi-Rename Tool: a button that puts [N1-3], the old name's first three letters, into the mask. Keep [N1-3] as it is. Keep it short.

rename.field.time.description: Multi-Rename Tool: a button that puts the file's time (hours, minutes, seconds) into the mask. Keep [h][m][s] as it is. Keep it short.

rename.first_only.description: Multi-Rename Tool: a checkbox for Search for, only its first match replaced. Keep it short.

rename.in_archive.description: Warning when the Multi-Rename Tool is used inside an archive.
rename.in_archive.message: Files inside archives cannot be renamed yet.

rename.mask.description: Multi-Rename Tool: the label above the name mask field ([N], [C]…). Keep it short.

rename.match_case.description: Multi-Rename Tool: a checkbox for Search for. Keep it short.

rename.new_name.description: Multi-Rename Tool: the heading of the list's new names. Keep it short.

rename.not_renamed_back.description: Error of a failed multi-rename that could not undo all it had done. {from} is the file that failed ("a.txt"); {err} the system's error; {names} the files left renamed, as "b.txt (was a.txt)", separated by commas.

rename.not_utf8.description: Warning when some chosen names cannot be shown in the Multi-Rename Tool.
rename.not_utf8.message: Names that are not UTF-8 are left out.

rename.old_name.description: Multi-Rename Tool: the heading of the list's old names. Keep it short.

rename.problem.bad_character.description: Multi-Rename Tool: after a new name in the list, in brackets, when it has a slash or another character file names cannot have. Keep it short.

rename.problem.exists.description: Multi-Rename Tool: after a new name in the list, in brackets, when another file in the folder has it. Keep it short.

rename.problem.no_name.description: Multi-Rename Tool: after a new name in the list, in brackets, when it is empty. Keep it short.

rename.problem.twice.description: Multi-Rename Tool: after a new name in the list, in brackets, when two files would get it. Keep it short.

rename.regex.description: Multi-Rename Tool: a checkbox for Search for, the text is a regular expression. Keep it short.

rename.regex_error.description: Multi-Rename Tool: shown in the list when the search text is not a valid regular expression. {err} is the regex library's own explanation (in English).

rename.replace.description: Multi-Rename Tool: the label above what the found text is replaced with. Keep it short.

rename.search.description: Multi-Rename Tool: the label above the text to search for in the names. Keep it short.

rename.start.description: Multi-Rename Tool: the button that renames, as Total Commander's. Keep it short.

rename.status.failed.description: Multi-Rename Tool: the status line when renaming failed and what was done was undone. {err} is the error ("a.txt: Permission denied").

rename.status.ready.description: Multi-Rename Tool: the status line before renaming; Start is the button "Start!".

rename.status.renamed.description: Multi-Rename Tool: the status line after renaming. {count} is how many files were renamed (12).

rename.status.took_back.description: Multi-Rename Tool: the status line after Undo. {count} is how many files got their old names back (12).

rename.step.description: Multi-Rename Tool: the label above the counter's step. Keep it short.

rename.undo.description: Multi-Rename Tool: the button that gives the files their old names back. Keep it short.

rename.was.description: One of the files a failed multi-rename could not give back its name: {to} its name now ("b.txt"), {from} its old one ("a.txt").

rename.with_extension.description: Multi-Rename Tool: a checkbox for Search for, the extension searched too. Keep it short.

scmd.column.modified.description: scmd (the terminal app), a panel's column title over the files' last modified time; centred in 16 columns, longer is cut: keep it short.

scmd.column.name.description: scmd (the terminal app), a panel's column title over the file names.

scmd.column.size.description: scmd (the terminal app), a panel's column title over the file sizes; centred in 10 columns, longer is cut: keep it short.

scmd.column.up_dir.description: scmd (the terminal app), shown in the Size column of the ".." row that leads to the parent folder, as Midnight Commander does; at most 10 columns.

scmd.command_line.not_on_server.description: scmd (the terminal app), error when a command is typed in the command line while the panel shows a server's folder.
scmd.command_line.not_on_server.message: Commands run on this computer, not on the server.

scmd.compare.marked.description: scmd (the terminal app), message after Compare Directories marked files. {count} is how many, e.g. 3.
scmd.compare.marked.message: {count, plural, one {# file marked: newer than, or missing on, the other side.} other {# files marked: newer than, or missing on, the other side.}}

scmd.compare.same.description: scmd (the terminal app), message after Compare Directories found no file to mark.
scmd.compare.same.message: The folders have the same files.

scmd.copying.description: scmd (the terminal app), message while a server's or an archive's file is copied out to be viewed or edited. {name} is the file's name, e.g. "report.pdf".

scmd.dialog.buttons.description: scmd (the terminal app), the line at the bottom of its dialogs: the keys that confirm and cancel. Enter and Esc are key names, keep them as they are; translate OK and Cancel.

scmd.editor.exists.description: sedit (scmd's text editor in the terminal), Save As: the file name typed is another file that exists. {name} is its path. The buttons under it are Overwrite and Cancel.

scmd.editor.file_name.description: sedit (scmd's text editor in the terminal), Save As dialog: the label of the line where the file's name (or path) is typed.

scmd.editor.key_bar.mark.description: sedit (scmd's text editor in the terminal), the key bar's F3, at most 6 characters: starts marking a block of text, and again ends it, as in Midnight Commander's editor.

scmd.editor.key_bar.replace.description: sedit (scmd's text editor in the terminal), the key bar's F4, at most 6 characters (as Midnight Commander's own "Replac"): replaces text (opens the Replace dialog).

scmd.editor.key_bar.save.description: sedit (scmd's text editor in the terminal), the key bar's F2, at most 6 characters: saves the file.

scmd.editor.replace.all.description: sedit (scmd's text editor in the terminal), Replace: button that replaces this match and all the rest without asking (matches, feminine where it matters).

scmd.editor.replace.ask.description: sedit (scmd's text editor in the terminal), Replace: the question asked at each match found, as Midnight Commander's editor asks. The buttons under it: Replace, All, Skip, Cancel.

scmd.editor.replace.done.description: sedit (scmd's text editor in the terminal), message after Replace: how many matches were replaced.

scmd.editor.replace.one.description: sedit (scmd's text editor in the terminal), Replace: button that replaces the match asked about, then goes on to the next.

scmd.editor.replace.skip.description: sedit (scmd's text editor in the terminal), Replace: button that leaves this match as it is and goes on to the next.

scmd.editor.replace.title.description: sedit (scmd's text editor in the terminal), the Replace dialog's title: what is searched for is replaced by other text.

scmd.editor.replace.with.description: sedit (scmd's text editor in the terminal), Replace dialog: the label of the line where the replacement text is typed.

scmd.editor.untitled.description: sedit (scmd's text editor in the terminal): the name shown for a new file that has no name yet (started without a file name).

scmd.error.read_settings.description: scmd (the terminal app), error at the start. {err} is the system's own error text, e.g. "Permission denied (os error 13)".

scmd.error.read_skin.description: scmd (the terminal app), error at the start when the theme chosen in the settings or with -S cannot be used. {name} is the theme's name as given, e.g. "pastel-night" (a Midnight Commander skin); {err} is the system's own error text, e.g. "entity not found".

scmd.error.read_tabs.description: scmd (the terminal app), error at the start when the tabs open last time cannot be read. {err} is the system's own error text, e.g. "Permission denied (os error 13)".
scmd.error.read_tabs.message: Could not read the open tabs: {err}

scmd.error.read_workspaces.description: scmd (the terminal app), error at the start when the saved workspaces (named sets of tabs) cannot be read. {err} is the system's own error text, e.g. "Permission denied (os error 13)".

scmd.error.running_here.description: scmd (the terminal app), printed when scmd is started inside the shell scmd itself opened (Ctrl+O), or from its command line: it does not start a second time there. scmd, Ctrl+O and exit (a shell command) stay as they are.
scmd.error.running_here.message: scmd is already running in this terminal. Press Ctrl+O, or type exit, to go back to it.

scmd.error.save_back.description: scmd (the terminal app), error when an edited copy of a server's or an archive's file cannot be put back there. {err} is the error's own text, e.g. "Connection refused (os error 111)".

scmd.error.save_searches.description: scmd (the terminal app), file viewer: error when the Find dialog's search history cannot be saved. {err} is the system's own error text, e.g. "Permission denied (os error 13)".

scmd.error.save_tabs.description: scmd (the terminal app), error printed in the terminal after scmd quits, when its open tabs cannot be saved. {err} is the system's own error text, e.g. "Permission denied (os error 13)".
scmd.error.save_tabs.message: Could not save the open tabs: {err}

scmd.error.view_nothing.description: Printed when sview (scmd's file viewer on its own, started as sview or scmd -v) is started without a file. sview and notes.txt stay as they are: notes.txt is an example file name.
scmd.error.view_nothing.message: Which file? Give its name, as in: sview notes.txt

scmd.find.backwards.description: scmd (the terminal app), file viewer's Find dialog: check box to search towards the start of the file.

scmd.find.case_sensitive.description: scmd (the terminal app), file viewer's Find dialog: check box to tell capital and small letters apart.

scmd.find.hex.description: scmd (the terminal app), file viewer's Find dialog: check box to search for bytes typed in hexadecimal; keep the example bytes as they are.

scmd.find.not_found.description: scmd (the terminal app), file viewer: message when Find finds nothing. {text} is what was searched for, e.g. "hello".

scmd.find.regex.description: scmd (the terminal app), file viewer's Find dialog: check box to search with a regular expression.

scmd.find.search_for.description: scmd (the terminal app), file viewer's Find dialog: label over the line where the text to find is typed.

scmd.find.title.description: scmd (the terminal app), title of the file viewer's Find dialog (F7).

scmd.find.whole_words.description: scmd (the terminal app), file viewer's Find dialog: check box to find only whole words.

scmd.group.files.description: scmd (the terminal app), Select group and Unselect group dialogs (+ and - keys): label over the line of file name patterns. Keep the patterns *.txt *.md and the / as they are.

scmd.group.select_title.description: scmd (the terminal app), title of the dialog that selects the files matching patterns (the + key, as in Midnight Commander).

scmd.group.unselect_title.description: scmd (the terminal app), title of the dialog that unselects the files matching patterns (the - key, as in Midnight Commander).

scmd.key_bar.copy.description: F5: scmd's function key bar at the bottom of the screen, as Midnight Commander's; each label has about 6 columns at 80 columns wide and is cut in the middle with ~ beyond that: keep it as short as possible.

scmd.key_bar.delete.description: F8: scmd's function key bar at the bottom of the screen, as Midnight Commander's; each label has about 6 columns at 80 columns wide and is cut in the middle with ~ beyond that: keep it as short as possible.

scmd.key_bar.edit.description: F4: scmd's function key bar at the bottom of the screen, as Midnight Commander's; each label has about 6 columns at 80 columns wide and is cut in the middle with ~ beyond that: keep it as short as possible.

scmd.key_bar.menu.description: F9, the menus: scmd's function key bar at the bottom of the screen, as Midnight Commander's; each label has about 6 columns at 80 columns wide and is cut in the middle with ~ beyond that: keep it as short as possible.

scmd.key_bar.mkdir.description: F7, a new folder: scmd's function key bar at the bottom of the screen, as Midnight Commander's; each label has about 6 columns at 80 columns wide and is cut in the middle with ~ beyond that: keep it as short as possible.

scmd.key_bar.move.description: F6, move or rename: scmd's function key bar at the bottom of the screen, as Midnight Commander's; each label has about 6 columns at 80 columns wide and is cut in the middle with ~ beyond that: keep it as short as possible.

scmd.key_bar.quit.description: F10, leaves scmd: scmd's function key bar at the bottom of the screen, as Midnight Commander's; each label has about 6 columns at 80 columns wide and is cut in the middle with ~ beyond that: keep it as short as possible.

scmd.key_bar.view.description: F3, the file viewer: scmd's function key bar at the bottom of the screen, as Midnight Commander's; each label has about 6 columns at 80 columns wide and is cut in the middle with ~ beyond that: keep it as short as possible.

scmd.message.error.description: scmd (the terminal app), title on the frame of a message box that tells of an error.

scmd.message.ok.description: scmd (the terminal app), the button under a message box, shown as [ OK ]; any key closes it. Keep it short.

scmd.music.keys.description: scmd (the terminal app), the line under a song's bars in the viewer. Space, ←→, +− and M are keys: keep them and their order; translate the word after each (pause, seek back and forth by 5 seconds, change the volume, mute). Keep it short: it shows only when the line has room.
scmd.music.keys.message: Space Pause  ←→ Seek  +− Volume  M Mute

scmd.not_yet.description: scmd (the terminal app), message when something the window version has is chosen that scmd cannot do yet. {what} tells what it is: menus (F9), file_operations (copy, move, delete, new folder), servers (connect, disconnect) or other (any other command); translate each sentence, not the words before the braces.

sidebar.group.bookmarks.description: Sidebar › Places: heading of a group of places, in small letters above it. Keep it short. The folders the user bookmarked.

sidebar.group.devices.description: Sidebar › Places: heading of a group of places, in small letters above it. Keep it short. Phones and cameras, also those paired through KDE Connect.

sidebar.group.drives.description: Sidebar › Places: heading of a group of places, in small letters above it. Keep it short. This computer's disks, cards and USB sticks.

sidebar.group.network.description: Sidebar › Places: heading of a group of places, in small letters above it. Keep it short. Network shares the system mounted.

sidebar.section.connections.description: Sidebar section heading (one section open at a time: its name in a list of them, or its icon's tooltip in a row of them). Keep it short. Holds the saved servers (SFTP, FTP, WebDAV…).

sidebar.section.folders.description: Sidebar section heading (one section open at a time: its name in a list of them, or its icon's tooltip in a row of them). Keep it short. Holds this computer's folders as a tree.

sidebar.volume.locked.description: Grey note beside a name in Sidebar › Places, in small letters. Keep it short; lower case as it follows the name. An encrypted disk not unlocked yet.

sidebar.volume.unmount_failed.description: Error unmounting a disk. {err} is the system's own error text.

split.bad_size.description: Error when the Split File dialog's part size cannot be read. {size} is what was typed ("ten"); the examples after the colon are what it understands, keep them as they are.

split.choose.description: Warning when Files › Split File is used without the cursor on a file.

split.dialog_title.description: Title of the Files › Split File dialog.

split.title.description: Title of the job that splits a file into parts, in the operation queue. {name} is the file's name ("movie.mkv").

sync.close.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): button that closes the window. Keep it short.

sync.column.date.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): column title of a side's modification time, left and right. Keep it short.

sync.column.name.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): column title of the items' paths. Keep it short.

sync.column.size.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): column title of a side's size, left and right; the column is narrow (90 px). Keep it short.

sync.compare.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): button that compares the two folders again. Keep it short.

sync.confirm.copy_left.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): one item of the comma-separated list in the question before synchronizing. {count}: number of items, e.g. 3; {size}: their size, e.g. 1.2 MB.

sync.confirm.copy_right.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): one item of the comma-separated list in the question before synchronizing. {count}: number of items, e.g. 3; {size}: their size, e.g. 1.2 MB.

sync.confirm.delete_left.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): one item of the comma-separated list in the question before synchronizing. {count}: number of items, e.g. 2.

sync.confirm.delete_right.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): one item of the comma-separated list in the question before synchronizing. {count}: number of items, e.g. 2.

sync.confirm.text.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): the question before synchronizing. {actions}: the list of what is done, e.g. Copy 3 to the right (1.2 MB), Delete 2 on the left. {trash} is yes when something is deleted: then the sentence about the trash is added (mind its leading space).

sync.error.changed.message: changed since the comparison; compare again

sync.error.compare.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): status line when the comparison failed. {err}: the system's error, e.g. Permission denied.

sync.error.no_folders.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): warning when a panel shows an archive or search results, so the window does not open.

sync.left.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): label before the left panel's folder at the top; the label column is narrow (44 px). Keep it short.

sync.mask.label.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): label before the file mask field (e.g. *.txt;*.md). Keep it short.

sync.option.asymmetric.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): checkbox: what differs goes right, and what only the right side has is deleted.
sync.option.asymmetric.message: Asymmetric (right becomes a copy of left)

sync.option.by_content.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): checkbox: files of the same size are read and compared, not their times trusted. Keep it short.

sync.option.ignore_date.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): checkbox: the files' times are not compared. Keep it short.

sync.option.subfolders.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): checkbox: compare the folders inside too. Keep it short.

sync.result.done.description: The operations queue: result of a finished Synchronize Dirs job. {count}: number of items done, e.g. 12.

sync.result.failed.message: {count, plural, one {# not synchronized} other {# not synchronized}}; {first}

sync.right.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): label before the right panel's folder at the top; the label column is narrow (44 px). Keep it short.

sync.show.label.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): label before the checkboxes choosing which items are listed. Keep it short.

sync.show.other.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): checkbox after Show: list the files that differ but nothing is done with. Keep the ≠. Keep it short.

sync.show.to_left.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): checkbox after Show: list what is copied to the left. Keep the arrow. Keep it short.

sync.show.to_right.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): checkbox after Show: list what is copied to the right. Keep the arrow. Keep it short.

sync.status.both_empty.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): status line when neither folder has anything to compare.

sync.status.comparing.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): status line at the bottom while comparing. {folder}: the folder being compared, below both sides, e.g. docs/2026, or ... at the start.

sync.status.counts.message: {right} to copy right, {left} to copy left, {delete} to delete, {equal} equal, {alone} left alone

sync.status.stopped.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): status line when the comparison was stopped.

sync.stop.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): button that stops a comparison, in place of Compare. Keep it short.

sync.synchronize.description: Synchronize Dirs window (Commands › Synchronize Dirs): button at the bottom that asks, then does what the list says. Keep it short.
